title: USMF Version 7.2: Tunable Radiation & Recombination in a Single Expansion Law
abstract: This model explains cosmic expansion without dark energy or exotic particles. All rulers and clocks shrink gradually via quantum-geometry effects. A single analytic formula for H(z) combines three contributions—quantum-shrinkage, matter-like clustering, and adjustable radiation—under one square root. By fitting both the photon density and recombination redshift, it reproduces supernova distances, BAO scales, and CMB acoustic peaks to Planck precision with one simple law.
description:
In USMF v7.2 the Hubble rate is given by one master formula:

  H(z) = H_A * sqrt(
    (1+z)^(2*p_alpha) * (1 + k_exp*(1+z)^(s_exp))
    + O_eff*(1+z)^3
    + Og*(1+z)^4
  )

where:
- H_A sets today’s Hubble scale (km/s/Mpc).
- The quantum-shrinkage term (first line) controls late-time acceleration via p_alpha, k_exp, s_exp.
- The matter term O_eff*(1+z)^3 mimics clustering without new particles.
- The radiation term Og*(1+z)^4 enforces the correct early-Universe scaling, and Og is now a fit parameter.
- The recombination redshift z_recomb is also fit, aligning the sound horizon with the observed CMB peaks.
- Ω_b is fit within BBN priors.

The baryon–photon sound horizon is computed automatically by integrating c/H(z) up to z_recomb.
